slot.brief: Present 3–4 statements on structures/hybridisation/hydrolysis of XeF2, XeF4, XeF6 (and their hydrolysis products) and ask how many are correct; make one statement subtly wrong on hydrolysis.

stem: Consider these statements about xenon fluorides and their hydrolysis. How many are correct? I. In $\text{XeF}_2$, three equatorial lone pairs give a linear shape and $sp^3d$ hybridisation. II. $\text{XeF}_4$ is square planar with two opposite lone pairs and $sp^3d^2$ hybridisation. III. $\text{XeF}_6$ is distorted octahedral; its controlled hydrolysis can give square-pyramidal $\text{XeOF}_4$, see-saw $\text{XeO}_2\text{F}_2$, and finally $\text{XeO}_3$, with xenon remaining in the $+6$ oxidation state. IV. Complete hydrolysis of $\text{XeF}_2$ gives xenon and oxygen in a $1:1$ molar ratio, besides HF.

verdicts.working: I, II and III are correct. Complete hydrolysis of XeF₂ is 2XeF₂ + 2H₂O → 2Xe + O₂ + 4HF, so Xe:O₂ is 2:1, not 1:1. Thus three statements are correct.

working:
I, II and III are correct. $2\text{XeF}_2+2\text{H}_2\text{O}\rightarrow2\text{Xe}+4\text{HF}+\text{O}_2$; hence $n(\text{Xe}):n(\text{O}_2)=2:1$, so IV is false.

Independent check: I, II and III are correct. Complete hydrolysis of XeF₂ is 2XeF₂ + 2H₂O → 2Xe + O₂ + 4HF, so Xe:O₂ is 2:1, not 1:1. Thus three statements are correct.
solution:
For XeF₂, XeF₄ and XeF₆, the stated shapes, hybridisations and controlled hydrolysis products in I–III are correct; xenon remains at $+6$ in the XeF₆ hydrolysis sequence.
$$2\text{XeF}_2+2\text{H}_2\text{O}\rightarrow2\text{Xe}+\text{O}_2+4\text{HF}$$
Thus $n(\text{Xe}):n(\text{O}_2)=2:1$, so IV is false. Three statements are correct.
